assumptions: Outer uprights 2.50 m, working crossbeam 1.83 m, width .62 m, floor-rail depth 1.22 m, profile 20 mm and carriage details are editable photo estimates. Earlier 6 ft/4 ft rectangle was not a measurement of these distinct spans.
The product listing is black/grey; white is retained from photographs of the user’s hardware. Exact variant equivalence is not established.
Five connected flared pockets form each hollow tier with circular net-basket seats. Curves, tilt, wall thickness, coupling geometry and basket dimensions are unmeasured photo fits.
Alternating 36 degree indexing is inferred from visible staggered pockets, not measured.
Caster height, lid thickness and top collar height are assumptions. Tier pitch is constrained by the stated overall height.
Reservoir-body 20 cm dimension is interpreted as excluding casters; updated hardware dimensions may change the stack-up.
Two arms share a carriage. Frame and reservoir remain anchored; no tipping, wheels, reservoir water, irrigation or structural flex dynamics are modeled.
Lift force and speed limits remain unmeasured priors. No harvest policies or tool adapters are transferred.
One V4 plant retains prior mechanics at a basket mouth. Growth at that angle and holder-root compliance are uncalibrated.
Four fore/aft side-plane braces replace the invented rear X. Posts extend above the working crossbeam.
Green guide blocks and black faceplate follow photos; exact bearing mechanism, bolt pitch, preload and tolerances are unmeasured.
Motor/gearhead, belt, brackets and fasteners are geometric approximations, not identified supplier parts or manufactured drawings.
Finite lift dynamics use a 2.8 kg carriage prior. Frame is anchored and rigid; bracing load, tipping, belt mechanics and real drive capacity remain unvalidated.
Counterweight function and opposite travel are user-confirmed; a 1:1 taut closed-belt transmission is an unmeasured mechanism interpretation.
The rear weight has its own backplate and rear guide shoes. The front shoe channel is opened at the rear so the two sliders can pass. Hidden attachment and bearing details are hypotheses.
Rear mass is a 2.8 kg prior, not a measurement. SO-101/YAM variants retain this counterweight and add arms only to the front carriage.
The direct shaft connecting rear weight to front plate in V3 was wrong and is removed. The weight shaft ends at its own rear carrier.
Coupling and pulley rotation are physical solver constraints, not replay transforms; belt stretch, slip and tooth contact are not simulated.
Stroke is restricted to 0.20–1.48 m on each slider so the rear weight also stays above the floor.
Provisional compact horizontal SO101 bracket; mounting interface needs confirmation.
Deck 360 x 130 x 6 mm; arm-base centers 240 mm apart; stock root plane offset compensated.
User supplied AEROBERRY v0.4 replaces left stock jaw assembly. Original user CAD preserved; compliant grip/cut dynamics not implemented.
